description: One generation's chain (wire 7.5-7.7) for alice's account, service key from keys.json: two identity.json deliveries (the account's first document, version 1, then version 3), a two-operation batch, an inbox entry at seq 5 (not chained), a one-operation batch creating a record (version (1, 6)), a two-operation batch updating it (version (1, 8)), and a service transition. item_hash = BLAKE3(lp("paykit/v1/item", item type, signed document bytes)); chain_hash = BLAKE3(lp("paykit/v1/chain", prev_chain_hash, envelope bytes)), starting from 32 zero bytes. The rejections are chains a verifier must refuse: the partial batch and the repeated batch ID have intact links, so only the batch rules catch them. batch_id_window repeats the record's batch, ID and all, gap_ms after its first stub's server_time: a verifier refuses it while gap_ms < 2592000000 (30 days) and accepts it from exactly 30 days on (wire 7.6).

rejections.name: partial batch
rejections.rule: a batch's operations take consecutive seqs (wire 7.4)

rejections.name: batch cut off at the end of a page
rejections.rule: a feed page never ends inside a batch (wire 8.4.4)

rejections.name: repeated batch ID
rejections.rule: a new batch whose ID is that of an earlier batch, with t_new - t_old < 30 days (2592000000 ms) by the server_time of each batch's first stub, is a repeat (wire 7.4, 7.6)

rejections.error: chain broken: seq 6 doesn't extend the previous chain hash
rejections.name: gap
rejections.rule: each stub extends the previous chain hash (wire 7.6)

rejections.error: rollback or fork: head at seq 3 doesn't match the chain
rejections.name: forked head
rejections.rule: a head at a seq already verified matches its chain hash (wire 7.7)

transition_proofs.name: record.put update (seq 8): the new version is (1, 8)
record.put create (seq 6): the record's first version is (1, 6)
identity.json delivery (seq 1): the account's first document, version 1
